A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, principal bounds, and original experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Appendix B reports original GPT-2 experiments on synthetic regression mixtures, including pretraining sweeps, predictive MSE, and parameter-estimation results in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the original experiments and add power-law fitting results and a three-family regression experiment with varying observation noise.

M1.justification: The uniform-attention encoder, mean pooling, decoder, squared-loss training objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The empirical GPT-2 architecture is also retained; shortened network formulas and relocated regularity explanations do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: The original linear/tanh regression mixture remains. Appendix B adds a three-family mixture incorporating the feature map x*|x| and evaluates noisier contexts, providing a limited extension within synthetic regression.

E2.justification: Table 1 introduces N-only and p-only power-law surrogates as comparators to the theory-motivated joint scaling model. Bayes (mixture) and Bayes (oracle) remain the predictive baselines, including in the added three-family experiment.

E3.justification: v3 adds pooled fitting across the N/p sweeps with R² evaluation, plus a noise sweep over 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 with results at selected context lengths. The original model size, training budgets, sweep grids, and evaluation sample counts are retained.

E4.justification: Two substantive analyses are added: testing coupled p–N scaling against single-variable explanations, and testing task-identification robustness in a harder three-family mixture under increasing noise. The latter directly measures wrong-family posterior mass alongside predictive errors; the original parameter-probing analysis remains.

E5.justification: Section 4 newly reports statistical fitting of power-law models to pooled Bayes-gap measurements. Existing averaging over 1,000 test prompts and 2,000 probing sets is retained; no new training-seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports R² values of 0.912, 0.030, and 0.016 for joint, N-only, and p-only fits. Table 2 adds posterior-mass and MSE results; at noise 0.5 and k=5, Transformer/mixture/oracle MSEs are 0.338/0.317/0.314. These are additional analyses and settings; the original two-family curves and findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E revises the mixture Hölder argument, removing explicit gating/modulus bounds and presenting a more explicit high-probability posterior-concentration bound. Appendix F adds filtration conditioning and dominating-measure reasoning. The principal risk identity, generalization rates, posterior-variance bound, and OOD bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 presents the risk decomposition as a central introduced contribution; v3 explicitly treats it as a classical identity used by the analysis. v3 also qualifies the abstract and contribution claims with uniform attention, while retaining the joint-scaling, task-adaptation, and OOD claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains the obstacle posed by prompt-dependent softmax attention and discusses extensions beyond finitely many task families. It interprets the new fits as qualitative, order-level support rather than evidence of tight constants or exponents. The original task-identification and within-family-learning interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies Gaussian inputs, clarifies that Bayes-gap evaluation uses squared differences, and documents the added feature map and noise levels. The earlier reference-implementation URL and MIT-license footnote are removed. Existing GPT-2 and Adam configuration details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Mukherjee et al. (2021), removes the Gemini Team citation, and replaces generic complementarity with Ma et al. (2025) by a specific softmax-versus-uniform-attention distinction. Describing the risk identity as classical also refines the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 introduces a dedicated main-text Experiments section, substantially rewrites the conclusion and practical discussion, and revises explanations throughout the setup, analysis, and appendices. It also adds an Impact Statement and removes Appendix J's LLM-proofreading disclosure.

P2.justification: The document changes globally from one-column to two-column layout, with reflowed equations and resized displays. v3 adds Tables 1–2 and a composite main-text Figure 2, while retaining v2 Figures 2–3 as smaller Appendix Figures 3–4.

improvement.justification: v3 better distinguishes the classical identity, architecture-specific guarantees, and GPT-2 empirical evidence. Tables 1–2 add targeted checks of scaling and noise sensitivity, strengthening support beyond the original illustrative curves. These gains are limited by incomplete specification of the three-family experiment and removal of the reference-implementation link; the central theoretical results remain unchanged.
